Typed decisions — Verdict, and Laya as the embedded open-source decision model ​

Why a decision engine ​

An agent makes thousands of judgements that are not prose: which domain handles this message, is this reply a plain yes, which of these options did the user mean, is it safe to call the write tool, how severe is this report. Answering them with a generative model is slow, expensive, verbose and uncalibrated — and routing them through prompt rules is unreliable.

A typed decision is a question with a fixed answer shape, answered with a probability distribution:

typequestionanswer
choicepick one of named options (criteria: {key: description})choice, probabilities, confidence
noulis this statement true?noul = P(true), confidence = |2p−1|
scorewhich ordinal level? (criteria: [levels])score (expected level), level, probabilities, confidence

This is the System One protocol (POST /v1/systemone {state, questions}), spoken by the proprietary Jev API and by Laya, an open-weight, Apache-2.0 decision model from Convai Innovations (github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya): ModernBERT-large / mmBERT-base encoders that answer in a single forward pass (~30 ms per question on a GPU, 100+ languages in the multilingual checkpoint, a laya-typed-decisions checkpoint fine-tuned for agent workflows).

What @marg-adk/verdict gives you ​

  • Backends behind one interface: rulesBackend (regex / predicates — free, certain, first), systemOneBackend (Laya via Ollama or laya-serve, or any compatible server), llmBackend (a generative model answering one letter, with logprobs → a real distribution; a bare letter → an honest low-confidence one-hot), mockBackend (tests).
  • A cascade: each question travels down the chain until answered with confidence ≥ the threshold; a dead link is skipped and counted; low-confidence earlier answers survive as a flagged fallback; answered_by says who answered what.
  • A Decider facade: choose, yesNo, score, decide, decideSchema (a JSON-schema-like object with enums / booleans / bounded integers → values), per-question calibration and abstention (min_confidence → low_confidence, abstained).
  • Calibration maths: temperature scaling with a grid-search fit, accuracy / Brier / ECE and the abstention trade-off table, fitAbstentionThreshold(samples, targetPrecision).
  • A System One server (createSystemOneServer(backend)): serve ANY backend over the same protocol — tests, air-gapped deployments, a gradual migration from a hosted API.
  • A CLI (npm run verdict -- "<text>" --choice dept=a,b,c) and an MCP server (npm run verdict:mcp) for any agent that speaks MCP.

Inside the runtime, the router asks a choice over the domain cards (keywords first, then the decision model, then the LLM with logprobs), sticky to the active domain.

Running Laya ​

bash
# Ollama (≥ 0.40.0):
ollama pull laya                      # or laya:421m-typed-decisions-mlx-fp16 / laya:322m-multilingual-mlx-fp16
export VERDICT_SYSTEMONE_URL=http://localhost:11434 VERDICT_SYSTEMONE_MODEL=laya

# or the Python server:
python -m pip install "laya[serve]"
LAYA_PORT=8000 laya-serve             # POST /v1/systemone, /v1/systemone/batch, GET /models
export VERDICT_SYSTEMONE_URL=http://localhost:8000

docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml --profile decisions up -d starts an Ollama service and pulls the model.

Limits to design around: choice / score take 2–26 options (about 20 recommended — the published Banking77 score of 0.43 on 77 options is the reason); each question has a ~512-token budget shared by instructions, options and state (1024 on the typed-decisions and multilingual checkpoints); request bodies up to 64 KiB; batch up to 64 states. Published figures (the authors' own measurements, T4 GPU): typed-decisions benchmark 0.766 vs 0.727 for the hosted API, ECE 0.081, ~33 ms per question. Verify on your data.

Calibrate before you trust a threshold ​

Confidence is a property of the distribution, not the chance of being right. Build a labelled set from your own traffic (a few hundred decisions), run evaluate(), fit a temperature, choose the threshold that reaches the precision you need, and store it per question id in the Decider's calibration. Re-run when the model, the options or the traffic change.

Where NOT to use it ​

The create gate reads a yes by its whole content with rules only. A decision model may advise a reader on the model-handoff path; it must never loosen a gate where a false yes performs a write. The cascade's maxDepth exists for exactly this.
